conclusion: No newly verified primary statement requires a numerical change to the owned forecast. The most useful additions are current cross-vendor competition at the same buyer and the distinction between dollar TAM, package units and retained profit. Existing moderate conviction is warranted; stronger confidence or a higher target would exceed the evidence.

findings.locator: PDF pp3 and6, CEO CPU opportunity and CFO outlook
findings.source_fact: Intel projects server CPU TAM from $40B to more than $200B over five years, while separately expecting industry server CPU units to grow more than30% in2026 and2027. Supply constraints extend into2028.
findings.judgment: The dollar TAM includes price and mix. It cannot independently substantiate the physical-unit path, and the >30% statement is a floor-like management growth expectation, not a30% ceiling or a contradiction of TrendForce >40%.
findings.owned_assumption_action: Keep the explicit missing matched2028–30 unit forecast disclosure. No mechanical base change; do not use fivefold dollar TAM to erase it.
findings.materiality: high scope guardrail; current pitch already discloses the gap

findings.locator: PDF p1 server roadmap;p5 DCAI discussion
findings.source_fact: Clearwater Forest is shipping for revenue; Diamond Rapids is sampling for a2027 ramp. Growth spans hyperscale, enterprise and neocloud customers.
findings.judgment: This is affirmative evidence that the recovery is not only a proposed future product or one unnamed hyperscaler. It is not customer concentration, shipment allocation, yield or retained-price disclosure.
findings.owned_assumption_action: Retain near-term growth as an owned conditional forecast. No extra CPU growth, premium or margin increment is justified by counting announcements again.
findings.materiality: medium affirmative context suitable for defense

findings.locator: PDF p2 GPU and purpose-built discussion;p3 modular x86 discussion
findings.source_fact: Intel offers modular verified x86 CPU instances for custom workloads; new GPU customer engagements are progressing toward commitments.
findings.pitch_location: p3 Other DCAI and no separate GPU windfall
findings.judgment: Modular x86 is a potential response to custom silicon, but there are no disclosed customer fees, orders, margins or incremental revenue amounts here. GPU progression is not a secured purchase. Purpose-built growth is not identical to all Other DCAI.
findings.owned_assumption_action: Keep no separate GPU windfall and preserve Other scope warning. Do not add royalties or design-win revenue without a bridge.

findings.locator: October27 article, Complete Choice Across the World’s Leading Chips section
findings.source_fact: Oracle describes Nvidia Vera CPUs as generally available, upcoming E7 using6th Gen AMD EPYC, and planned multiyear Intel X14 using Diamond Rapids within one architecture-choice roadmap.
findings.additional_locator: October28 announcement, first paragraph: OCI Arm AGI CPU deployment planned for fall2027
findings.judgment: The primary buyer confirms simultaneous support for several architectures. An Intel deployment announcement supports access to demand, not exclusive customer retention. This is a new cross-source synthesis, not a new claim that Oracle uses competitors.
findings.owned_assumption_action: No automatic additional share cut beyond the existing50%→42% industry-share assumption. Monitor repeated purchased deployments and price/mix across generations; do not equate a partnership announcement with a moat.
findings.materiality: high defense context; ten-page pitch is not misleading without adding all product names

findings.locator: November3 CEO quote and Recent PR Highlights
findings.source_fact: AMD says Q4 growth accelerates as Helios and Venice production scale. Its Q3 Data Center revenue is$8.5B, up97%, combining EPYC processors with MI450 GPU demand. Q4 total-company revenue guidance is$17B.
findings.additional_locator: October27 article,6th Gen AMD EPYC for OCI Compute E7 and Acceleron NIC discussion
findings.additional_fact: AMD identifies agent orchestration, retrieval and caching among E7 workloads; Pensando offloads networking, storage and security to preserve host CPU capacity.
findings.judgment: Competition is contemporaneous, not only an older Turin benchmark. Aggregate AMD Data Center growth cannot identify EPYC unit share, CPU ASP or CPU profit. Networking offload also prevents a fixed CPU-per-accelerator demand identity.
findings.owned_assumption_action: Treat2027 Intel ASP and40% mature margin as conditional despite launch progress. No quantified reduction follows without matched EPYC units, workload allocation or customer economics.
findings.materiality: high qualitative opposing context; no proven numerical contradiction

findings.locator: MD&A pp28–29, Data Center and Client and Gaming paragraphs
findings.source_fact: Q3 Client units rose6% and ASP1%; YTD Client units rose21% and ASP fell2%, mainly mobile mix. Q3 Client revenue rose7%, whereas Client and Gaming together fell8%. Data Center revenue and operating profit combine EPYC and Instinct.
findings.judgment: Client & Gaming decline cannot be used as a PC-demand proxy. Data Center operating margin around34% cannot be treated as a CPU-only retained-margin comparator.
findings.owned_assumption_action: Parent owns PC forecast. No server margin calibration from this mixed segment. Explicitly flag the client-versus-gaming distinction if peer results are cited.
findings.materiality: medium scope protection; current pitch does not misuse these figures

findings.locator: Shareholder letter printed p2, Arm Is Gaining Share Across the Data Center;printed p3 opening
findings.source_fact: Arm says first AGI CPU commercial deliveries are on track for fiscalQ4FYE27, with up to$2B acrossFYE27–28. Its >60% calendar2026 server-share expectation applies to top hyperscalers.
findings.judgment: FiscalQ4FYE27 corresponds toJan–Mar2027; the$2B is a two-fiscal-year amount, not annualCY2027 sales. Top-hyperscaler share is not global server share; the cited passage does not fully define unit/revenue or new/installed denominator.
findings.owned_assumption_action: Do not combine this share mechanically with TrendForce global market shares. Existing competition stress remains; no extra numeric share deduction is supported.
findings.materiality: high if used in oral defense; no current pitch misuse

findings.locator: Corrected November4 transcript printed pp12–14, Lee Simpson/Vivek Arya/Joe Quatrochi Q&A
findings.source_fact: Arm sees pricing headroom on larger, higher-core CPUs, says supply remains tight, and reports having exercised pricing flexibility. It frames first AGI CPU gross margin around30–40%, with higher margins expected on later versions.
findings.judgment: This supports the mechanism of richer CPU package pricing under constrained supply. It also shows manufacturing, memory and partner cost pressure; higher package prices do not automatically produce an Intel profit moat. Arm gross margin is not Intel DCAI operating margin and the cost scopes differ.
findings.owned_assumption_action: No target increase. Keep the separately modeled retained-profit case and CPU expense sensitivity. This is corroboration of mechanism, not calibration of magnitude or duration.

findings.locator: Products MD&A pp33–34;Foundry MD&A p35;Note2 segment measurement
findings.source_fact: The reported Products and Foundry results support the recent profit and period-charge bridges already recorded in foundry_internal_recovery_cost_bridge.json. No new standalone CPU expense, Other DCAI profit or net SKU-price disclosure was located in this full-section reread.
findings.judgment: The selected model still lacks an observed cohort-level price/cost/retention bridge that jointly proves durable product profit and Foundry recovery. This is an identification limit, not evidence of an explicit duplicate forecast line.
findings.owned_assumption_action: Current p6 now correctly says further factory profit recovery remains a forecast. Keep all model assumptions and downside cases visible; do not credit historical Intel3/18A learning again.
